correctness.rationale: Independent squares force disjoint supports for the images of distinct basis elements, so any isomorphism is monomial and its permutation rotates the cycle. Ideal propagation by multiplication and squaring gives simplicity. The diagonal normalization and rotation equations close modulo 3: odd n allows exactly one choice of starting scale for each rotation and one class, while even n identifies the residual exponents by sign. In the twisted even case n=2m the two-step lift has m-th power the diagonal map with factors omega on even and omega^2 on odd indices; this includes n=2, when the lift is already diagonal. It follows that the full group is cyclic of order 3m and its order-3 subgroup is complemented iff 3 does not divide m. In the even balanced case a pure rotation splits the extension and conjugates the diagonal kernel by inversion. The cyclic idempotent equation gives 1, 3, and 0 nonzero solutions in the stated cases.
residual_risks: Finite replay is corroboration; the recurrence and group argument establish the unrestricted assertion. No group-scheme claim was checked.
